robot_model.description: Defines whether an individual robot is physically capable of executing at most one task at a time (ST) or multiple tasks simultaneously (MT).

ST.definition: Single-task robot: The robot can execute at most one task at any given instant, constrained by shared physical resources (single manipulator, chassis locomotion, or computational focus).
ST.example: A mobile warehouse robot with a single gripper carrying one container to a packing station.

MT.definition: Multi-task robot: The robot possesses independent hardware subsystems capable of executing multiple disjoint tasks simultaneously.
MT.example: A dual-arm mobile platform where one arm holds and inspects an item while the other arm sorts packages, or an autonomous vehicle mapping an environment while transporting cargo.

task_model.description: Defines whether each subtask can be performed by an individual robot (SR) or strictly requires a synchronized team/coalition of robots (MR).

SR.definition: Single-robot task: The task requires exactly one robot to perform it, falling within the physical and payload capabilities of a single agent.
SR.example: Transporting a 2.0 kg box when each available mobile robot has a maximum payload capacity of 10.0 kg.

MR.definition: Multi-robot task: The task requires a synchronized coalition of two or more robots, exceeding the payload capacity or physical capabilities of any single robot.
MR.example: Lifting and transporting a 20.0 kg heavy pallet when every individual robot in the fleet has a maximum payload limit of 10.0 kg.

time_horizon.description: Defines whether task allocation is instantaneous for immediate execution (IA) or time-extended planning over a future schedule (TA).

IA.definition: Instantaneous assignment: Allocation decisions are made in one immediate assignment event rather than being revised over a future schedule; an assigned task may still contain sequential subtasks or precedence constraints.
IA.example: 2 pickup tasks dispatched concurrently to 2 idle mobile robots with no sequential backlog or capacity bottlenecks.

TA.definition: Time-extended assignment: Tasks must be scheduled over time into a sequence or queue, due to task backlogs (|tasks| > |robots|), capacity bottlenecks forcing sequential trips, or multi-stop routing tours.
TA.example: 3 boxes need to be moved by 2 robots, requiring at least one robot to execute a subsequent trip over time.

dependency.description: Defines how task execution utilities and schedules interact: independent (ND), intra-schedule routing tours (ID), inter-schedule cross constraints (XD), or complex dependencies (CD).

ND.definition: No dependencies: The utility and execution of a task depend solely on the assigned robot and task itself, with no inter-task precedence or routing coupling (e.g. independent trips returning to origin).
ND.example: 2 independent mobile robots each picking up one box and returning to base, with zero ordering constraints between them.

ID.definition: In-schedule dependencies: The execution cost or order of tasks depends on other tasks assigned to the same robot's schedule (e.g. multi-stop routing where pickup sequence affects total travel distance).
ID.example: A single mobile robot picking up Box A and then Box B in a combined multi-stop route before returning to drop-off.

XD.definition: Cross-schedule dependencies: The execution or validity of a task depends on the schedule or status of tasks assigned to other robots (e.g. precedence ordering between robots or multi-robot coalition synchronization).
XD.example: Robot 2 must place the blue box only after Robot 1 has finished placing the red box, or two robots synchronizing to lift a heavy crate.

CD.definition: Complex dependencies: Task allocation problems for which agent-task utilities have inter-schedule dependencies for complex tasks (in addition to any in-schedule and cross-schedule dependencies for simple or compound tasks). The effective utility of an agent for a task depends on the schedules of other agents in a manner determined by the chosen task decomposition.
CD.example: Disaster response where fire trucks require routes cleared by bulldozers, but which debris piles must be cleared depends on the chosen routing and decomposition of fire tasks across the fleet.

ND[ST-SR-IA].name: No-Dependency Single-Task Single-Robot Instantaneous Assignment
ND[ST-SR-IA].theoretical_formulation: Linear Sum Assignment Problem (LSAP) (Votaw and Orden, 1952)
ND[ST-SR-IA].criteria: All tasks are SR (object weight <= single robot capacity), |qualified robots| >= |tasks| (all tasks executable concurrently), robots are ST, and no precedence or routing dependencies link the subtasks.
ND[ST-SR-IA].optimization_target: Minimizing total makespan or aggregate transit cost for one-to-one simultaneous dispatch.

ND[ST-SR-TA].name: No-Dependency Single-Task Single-Robot Time-Extended Assignment
ND[ST-SR-TA].theoretical_formulation: Can be reformulated as Linear Sum Assignment Problem (LSAP) (Korsah et al., 2013)
ND[ST-SR-TA].criteria: Tasks are independent and each is executable by a single robot with no cross-schedule or in-schedule routing dependencies, but the number of tasks exceeds available qualified robots (|tasks| > |qualified robots|) or capacity bottlenecks force robots to plan sequential trips over time.
ND[ST-SR-TA].optimization_target: Minimizing schedule makespan or weighted completion time across robot job queues.

ID[ST-SR-TA].name: In-Schedule Dependency Single-Task Single-Robot Time-Extended Assignment
ID[ST-SR-TA].theoretical_formulation: Multiple Traveling Salesman Problem (m-TSP) (Bektas, 2006) / Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP) (Toth and Vigo, 2001) / Scheduling on unrelated machines to minimize weighted sum of completion times (R || sum w_j C_j) (Brucker, 2011; Bruno et al., 1974)
ID[ST-SR-TA].criteria: A robot performs multi-stop routing tours (e.g. visiting multiple pickup locations before returning to drop-off or base), where the execution cost/time depends on the permutation/ordering of visits within that robot's individual schedule.
ID[ST-SR-TA].optimization_target: Minimizing cumulative tour distance or travel time across multi-stop routes.

XD[ST-SR-IA].name: Cross-Schedule Dependency Single-Task Single-Robot Instantaneous Assignment
XD[ST-SR-IA].theoretical_formulation: Assignment Problem with Side Constraints (APSC) (Mazzola and Neebe, 1986)
XD[ST-SR-IA].criteria: Tasks are executable by individual robots and can be dispatched concurrently, but inter-task precedence or cross-robot ordering constraints link the completion of a task on one robot's schedule to the start of a task on another robot's schedule.
XD[ST-SR-IA].optimization_target: Satisfying inter-robot precedence constraints while minimizing overall completion time.

XD[ST-SR-TA].name: Cross-Schedule Dependency Single-Task Single-Robot Time-Extended Assignment
XD[ST-SR-TA].theoretical_formulation: Scheduling, with precedence constraints, on unrelated machines to minimize weighted sum of completion times (R | prec | sum w_j C_j) (Brucker, 2001; Lenstra and Rinnooy Kan, 1978) / Vehicle Routing Problems with precedence or synchronization constraints (Bredström and Rönnqvist, 2007, 2008)
XD[ST-SR-TA].criteria: Tasks require multi-trip time-extended scheduling (|tasks| > |robots| or capacity limits) AND possess cross-schedule precedence dependencies linking different robots' temporal schedules.
XD[ST-SR-TA].optimization_target: Minimizing total schedule makespan under multi-trip robot routing and inter-robot temporal precedence.

XD[ST-MR-IA].name: Cross-Schedule Dependency Single-Task Multi-Robot Instantaneous Assignment
XD[ST-MR-IA].theoretical_formulation: Set Partitioning Problem (SPP) (Balas and Padberg, 1976) / Coalition Formation
XD[ST-MR-IA].criteria: At least one task exceeds single-robot capability or payload capacity (object weight > max single robot capacity), requiring a synchronized coalition of >= 2 robots working simultaneously in an immediate time horizon.
XD[ST-MR-IA].optimization_target: Selecting and synchronizing optimal multi-robot coalitions to execute heavy or complex tasks concurrently.

XD[ST-MR-TA].name: Cross-Schedule Dependency Single-Task Multi-Robot Time-Extended Assignment
XD[ST-MR-TA].theoretical_formulation: Multi-mode Multi-processor Task Scheduling (Brucker, 2001; Bianco et al., 1999) / Coalition Formation with Spatial and Temporal Constraints (CFSTP) (Ramchurn et al., 2010)
XD[ST-MR-TA].criteria: Multiple multi-robot tasks or multi-trip requirements necessitate scheduling multi-robot coalitions over an extended time horizon with cross-schedule synchronization.
XD[ST-MR-TA].optimization_target: Optimizing multi-agent coalition sequences, synchronization barriers, and makespan over extended time horizons.
